why: --fs-only promises only the checks that read the filesystem being scanned, and $HOME is this machine, not that filesystem. The 2026-11-16 field report found ~/.ssh/authorized_keys read anyway. Here the home holds the campaign's SSH key and a file at an implant install path, and the run is not told --home, so the home is the machine's own: neither may be read. If either were, the exit would be 2 and the promise false. Each section that was not read says so in a line, so a skipped check is never mistaken for a clean one (ADR-0069).
